disease_label_per_paper: Familial Mediterranean fever presenting as recurrent surgical abdomen
presentation_summary: 19-year-old British woman with no significant past medical history presented repeatedly over several months with abdominal pain, fever, and high inflammatory markers.

First admission was for 2 weeks of abdominal pain with fever, dysuria, and nausea; she was tachycardic at 130/min, blood pressure 117/89 mmHg, temperature 37.7 C, and had generalized guarding in the epigastrium and suprapubic region.

Admission labs showed WBC 12.7 x10^9/L, neutrophils 9.1 x10^9/L, platelets 419 x10^9/L, CRP 232 mg/L, hemoglobin 129 g/L, albumin 47 g/L, and creatinine 62 umol/L; urine and stool infectious studies were not diagnostic.
CT chest/abdomen/pelvis showed nonspecific mild fat stranding in the right distal paracolic gutter and ultrasound was unremarkable; she was discharged without a specific diagnosis.

She re-presented with recurrent abdominal pain and later with right-sided pleuritic chest pain and fever 38.4 C. Detailed history revealed 3 years of intermittent 2-5 day episodes, sometimes menstrual-associated, typically abdominal pain and occasionally pleuritic chest pain and fevers.
Genetic testing, colchicine response, mild pericarditis on later echocardiography, negative serologies/cultures, and the paper's final FMF diagnosis are preserved as confirmatory/non-ranking context.
